neighbours.label: ironic understatement: a phrase that pretends a serious problem is trivial (the small matter of, a minor detail, never mind the fact), peaking on its noun or quantifier
fire: Great plan, apart from the small matter of the missing forty million dollars.
Everyone cheered the launch, overlooking the minor detail that the rocket had exploded.
He says he is ready for the marathon, never mind the fact that he cannot walk.
Our landlord shrugged off the tiny issue of the collapsed ceiling.
There is just the little question of who will pay for the destroyed bridge.
Sure, the wedding went fine, if you ignore a few guests getting arrested.
She got the promotion, leaving aside the trifling matter of her forged degree.
They'll open on time, barring one small snag: the building is on fire.
quiet: The plan was approved, along with a budget of forty million dollars.
Everyone cheered the launch, and the engineers noted every detail of the rocket's flight.
He says he is ready for the marathon, and the fact is that he trained all year.
Our landlord repaired the small crack in the ceiling on Tuesday.
There is a question on the form about who will pay for the bridge.
The wedding went fine, and a few guests stayed to help with the chairs.
She got the promotion, and the matter of her salary was settled in May.
They'll open on time, since the small repairs to the building are finished.

notes: Card: scattered tokens (' fact', ' like', ' few', ' cozy', 'ops'). Output suppresses inconvenient, disappoint, quite. Probes: 'small matter of the unpaid rent' 1.06, 'minor detail' 0.79, 'never mind the fact' 0.58, 'a few broken windows' 0.57; sincere 'noted the fact' 0.04. Its - pole looks unrelated (narrative function words); I did not test that.
